en: # Programming a Guessing Game
zh: # 编写猜数字游戏

en: Let’s jump into Rust by working through a hands-on project together! This chapter introduces you to a few common Rust concepts by showing you how to use them in a real program. You’ll learn about `let`, `match`, methods, associated functions, external crates, and more! In the following chapters, we’ll explore these ideas in more detail. In this chapter, you’ll just practice the fundamentals.
zh: 让我们通过一起完成一个动手项目来进入 Rust 的世界！本章通过展示如何在一个真实程序中使用一些常见的 Rust 概念来介绍它们。你将了解 `let`、`match`、方法、关联函数、外部 crate 等等！在接下来的章节中，我们会更详细地探讨这些概念。在本章中，你只需练习这些基础知识。

en: We’ll implement a classic beginner programming problem: a guessing game. Here’s how it works: The program will generate a random integer between 1 and 100. It will then prompt the player to enter a guess. After a guess is entered, the program will indicate whether the guess is too low or too high. If the guess is correct, the game will print a congratulatory message and exit.
zh: 我们将实现一个经典的编程入门问题：猜数字游戏。它的工作方式如下：程序会生成一个 1 到 100 之间的随机整数，然后提示玩家输入猜测。输入猜测后，程序会指出猜测太低还是太高。如果猜对了，游戏会打印一条祝贺消息并退出。

en: ### Storing Values with Variables
zh: ### 用变量存储值

en: Next, we’ll create a *variable* to store the user input, like this:
zh: 接下来，我们将创建一个*变量*来存储用户输入，像这样：

en: Now the program is getting interesting! There’s a lot going on in this little line. We use the `let` statement to create the variable. Here’s another example:
zh: 现在程序变得有趣了！这一小行里发生了很多事情。我们使用 `let` 语句创建变量。这里还有一个例子：

en: This line creates a new variable named `apples` and binds it to the value `5`. In Rust, variables are immutable by default, meaning once we give the variable a value, the value won’t change. We’ll be discussing this concept in detail in the [“Variables and Mutability”](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-01-variables-and-mutability.html#variables-and-mutability) section in Chapter 3. To make a variable mutable, we add `mut` before the variable name:
zh: 这一行创建一个名为 `apples` 的新变量，并将其绑定到值 `5`。在 Rust 中，变量默认是不可变的，也就是说，一旦给变量赋值，该值就不会改变。我们将在第 3 章的[“变量与可变性”](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-01-variables-and-mutability.html#variables-and-mutability)一节中详细讨论这个概念。要使变量可变，我们在变量名之前加上 `mut`：

en:
```rust
let apples = 5; // immutable
let mut bananas = 5; // mutable
```
zh:
```rust
let apples = 5; // immutable
let mut bananas = 5; // mutable
```

en: Note: The `//` syntax starts a comment that continues until the end of the line. Rust ignores everything in comments. We’ll discuss comments in more detail in [Chapter 3](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-04-comments.html).
zh: 注意：`//` 语法开始一条持续到行末的注释。Rust 会忽略注释中的所有内容。我们将在[第 3 章](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-04-comments.html)更详细地讨论注释。

en: Returning to the guessing game program, you now know that `let mut guess` will introduce a mutable variable named `guess`. The equal sign (`=`) tells Rust we want to bind something to the variable now. On the right of the equal sign is the value that `guess` is bound to, which is the result of calling `String::new`, a function that returns a new instance of a `String`. [`String`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/string/struct.String.html) is a string type provided by the standard library that is a growable, UTF-8 encoded bit of text.
zh: 回到猜数字游戏程序：现在你知道 `let mut guess` 会引入一个名为 `guess` 的可变变量。等号（`=`）告诉 Rust 我们现在要把某个值绑定到该变量。等号右侧是 `guess` 绑定的值，即调用 `String::new` 的结果——这个函数返回一个新的 `String` 实例。[`String`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/string/struct.String.html) 是标准库提供的一种字符串类型，是可增长、UTF-8 编码的文本。

en: The `::` syntax in the `::new` line indicates that `new` is an associated function of the `String` type. An *associated function* is a function that’s implemented on a type, in this case `String`. This `new` function creates a new, empty string. You’ll find a `new` function on many types because it’s a common name for a function that makes a new value of some kind.
zh: `::new` 行中的 `::` 语法表示 `new` 是 `String` 类型的一个关联函数。*关联函数*是在某个类型上实现的函数，这里是 `String`。这个 `new` 函数创建一个新的空字符串。你会在许多类型上找到 `new` 函数，因为它是创建某种新值的函数的常见名称。

en: In full, the `let mut guess = String::new();` line has created a mutable variable that is currently bound to a new, empty instance of a `String`. Whew!
zh: 完整地说，`let mut guess = String::new();` 这一行创建了一个可变变量，当前绑定到一个新的空 `String` 实例。哇！

en: ### Receiving User Input
zh: ### 接收用户输入

en: Recall that we included the input/output functionality from the standard library with `use std::io;` on the first line of the program. Now we’ll call the `stdin` function from the `io` module, which will allow us to handle user input:
zh: 回想一下，我们在程序第一行用 `use std::io;` 引入了标准库中的输入/输出功能。现在我们调用 `io` 模块中的 `stdin` 函数，它允许我们处理用户输入：

en:
```rust
    io::stdin()
        .read_line(&mut guess)
```
zh:
```rust
    io::stdin()
        .read_line(&mut guess)
```

en: If we hadn’t imported the `io` module with `use std::io;` at the beginning of the program, we could still use the function by writing this function call as `std::io::stdin`. The `stdin` function returns an instance of [`std::io::Stdin`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/io/struct.Stdin.html), which is a type that represents a handle to the standard input for your terminal.
zh: 如果我们在程序开头没有用 `use std::io;` 导入 `io` 模块，我们仍然可以把函数调用写成 `std::io::stdin` 来使用它。`stdin` 函数返回一个 [`std::io::Stdin`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/io/struct.Stdin.html) 实例，这个类型表示终端标准输入的句柄。

en: Next, the line `.read_line(&mut guess)` calls the [`read_line`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/io/struct.Stdin.html#method.read_line) method on the standard input handle to get input from the user. We’re also passing `&mut guess` as the argument to `read_line` to tell it what string to store the user input in. The full job of `read_line` is to take whatever the user types into standard input and append that into a string (without overwriting its contents), so we therefore pass that string as an argument. The string argument needs to be mutable so that the method can change the string’s content.
zh: 接下来，`.read_line(&mut guess)` 这一行在标准输入句柄上调用 [`read_line`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/io/struct.Stdin.html#method.read_line) 方法，以获取用户输入。我们还把 `&mut guess` 作为参数传给 `read_line`，告诉它将用户输入存储到哪个字符串中。`read_line` 的完整工作是把用户输入到标准输入的所有内容追加到字符串中（不覆盖其内容），因此我们传入该字符串作为参数。字符串参数必须是可变的，这样该方法才能修改字符串内容。

en: The `&` indicates that this argument is a *reference*, which gives you a way to let multiple parts of your code access one piece of data without needing to copy that data into memory multiple times. References are a complex feature, and one of Rust’s major advantages is how safe and easy it is to use references. You don’t need to know a lot of those details to finish this program. For now, all you need to know is that, like variables, references are immutable by default. Hence, you need to write `&mut guess` rather than `&guess` to make it mutable. (Chapter 4 will explain references more thoroughly.)
zh: `&` 表示这个参数是一个*引用*，它让你能够让代码的多个部分访问同一份数据，而无需多次将该数据复制到内存中。引用是一个复杂的功能，而 Rust 的一大优势就是使用引用既安全又简单。你不需要了解很多这些细节就能完成这个程序。目前你只需要知道，和变量一样，引用默认是不可变的。因此，你需要写 `&mut guess` 而不是 `&guess`，使其可变。（第 4 章会更全面地解释引用。）

en: ### Handling Potential Failure with `Result`
zh: ### 用 `Result` 处理可能的失败

en: We’re still working on this line of code. We’re now discussing a third line of text, but note that it’s still part of a single logical line of code. The next part is this method:
zh: 我们仍然在处理这一行代码。现在讨论的是第三行文本，但请注意它仍然属于同一行逻辑代码。下一部分是这个方法：

en: We could have written this code as:
zh: 我们本可以这样写这段代码：

en: However, one long line is difficult to read, so it’s best to divide it. It’s often wise to introduce a newline and other whitespace to help break up long lines when you call a method with the `.method_name()` syntax. Now let’s discuss what this line does.
zh: 然而，一行太长难以阅读，所以最好将其拆分。当你使用 `.method_name()` 语法调用方法时，通常明智的做法是引入换行和其他空白，以帮助拆分过长的行。现在让我们讨论这一行的作用。

en: As mentioned earlier, `read_line` puts whatever the user enters into the string we pass to it, but it also returns a `Result` value. [`Result`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/result/enum.Result.html) is an [*enumeration*](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-00-enums.html), often called an *enum*, which is a type that can be in one of multiple possible states. We call each possible state a *variant*.
zh: 如前所述，`read_line` 把用户输入的内容放入我们传入的字符串中，但它也会返回一个 `Result` 值。[`Result`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/result/enum.Result.html) 是一种[*枚举*](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-00-enums.html)，通常称为 *enum*，它是一种可能处于多种状态之一的类型。我们把每种可能的状态称为一个*变体*（variant）。

en: [Chapter 6](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-00-enums.html) will cover enums in more detail. The purpose of these `Result` types is to encode error-handling information.
zh: [第 6 章](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-00-enums.html)会更详细地介绍枚举。这些 `Result` 类型的用途是编码错误处理信息。

en: `Result`’s variants are `Ok` and `Err`. The `Ok` variant indicates the operation was successful, and it contains the successfully generated value. The `Err` variant means the operation failed, and it contains information about how or why the operation failed.
zh: `Result` 的变体是 `Ok` 和 `Err`。`Ok` 变体表示操作成功，它包含成功生成的值。`Err` 变体表示操作失败，它包含关于操作如何或为何失败的信息。

en: Values of the `Result` type, like values of any type, have methods defined on them. An instance of `Result` has an [`expect` method](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/result/enum.Result.html#method.expect) that you can call. If this instance of `Result` is an `Err` value, `expect` will cause the program to crash and display the message that you passed as an argument to `expect`. If the `read_line` method returns an `Err`, it would likely be the result of an error coming from the underlying operating system. If this instance of `Result` is an `Ok` value, `expect` will take the return value that `Ok` is holding and return just that value to you so that you can use it. In this case, that value is the number of bytes in the user’s input.
zh: `Result` 类型的值，和任何类型的值一样，都有定义在其上的方法。`Result` 实例有一个可以调用的 [`expect` 方法](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/../std/result/enum.Result.html#method.expect)。如果这个 `Result` 实例是 `Err` 值，`expect` 会让程序崩溃并显示你传给 `expect` 的消息。如果 `read_line` 方法返回 `Err`，那很可能是底层操作系统产生的错误导致的。如果这个 `Result` 实例是 `Ok` 值，`expect` 会取出 `Ok` 持有的返回值，并将该值返回给你，以便你使用。在这种情况下，该值是用户输入中的字节数。

en: If you don’t call `expect`, the program will compile, but you’ll get a warning:
zh: 如果你不调用 `expect`，程序仍会编译，但你会收到一个警告：

```console
   |
   = note: this `Result` may be an `Err` variant, which should be handled
   = note: `#[warn(unused_must_use)]` (part of `#[warn(unused)]`) on by default
help: use `let _ = ...` to ignore the resulting value
   |
10 |     let _ = io::stdin().read_line(&mut guess);
   |     +++++++

warning: `guessing_game` (bin "guessing_game") generated 1 warning
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.59s
```
zh:
```console
$ cargo build
   Compiling guessing_game v0.1.0 (file:///projects/guessing_game)
warning: unused `Result` that must be used
  --> src/main.rs:10:5
   |
10 |     io::stdin().read_line(&mut guess);
   |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: this `Result` may be an `Err` variant, which should be handled
   = note: `#[warn(unused_must_use)]` (part of `#[warn(unused)]`) on by default
help: use `let _ = ...` to ignore the resulting value
   |
10 |     let _ = io::stdin().read_line(&mut guess);
   |     +++++++

warning: `guessing_game` (bin "guessing_game") generated 1 warning
```

en: Rust warns that you haven’t used the `Result` value returned from `read_line`, indicating that the program hasn’t handled a possible error.
zh: Rust 警告你没有使用 `read_line` 返回的 `Result` 值，表示程序没有处理可能发生的错误。

en: The right way to suppress the warning is to actually write error-handling code, but in our case we just want to crash this program when a problem occurs, so we can use `expect`. You’ll learn about recovering from errors in [Chapter 9](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch09-02-recoverable-errors-with-result.html).
zh: 抑制该警告的正确做法是实际编写错误处理代码，但在我们的情况下，我们只是想在发生问题时让程序崩溃，所以可以使用 `expect`。你将在[第 9 章](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch09-02-recoverable-errors-with-result.html)学习如何从错误中恢复。

In this case, we specify the `rand` crate with the semantic version specifier `0.10.1`. en: #### Ensuring Reproducible Builds
zh: #### 确保可重现的构建

en: Cargo has a mechanism that ensures that you can rebuild the same artifact every time you or anyone else builds your code: Cargo will use only the versions of the dependencies you specified until you indicate otherwise. For example, say that next week version 0.10.2 of the `rand` crate comes out, and that version contains an important bug fix, but it also contains a regression that will break your code. To handle this, Rust creates the *Cargo.lock* file the first time you run `cargo build`, so we now have this in the *guessing_game* directory.
zh: Cargo 有一种机制，确保你或任何其他人每次构建代码时都能重新构建出相同的产物：Cargo 只会使用你指定的依赖版本，直到你另行指示。例如，假设下周 `rand` crate 发布了 0.10.2 版本，该版本包含一个重要 bug 修复，但也包含一个会破坏你代码的回归问题。为处理这种情况，Rust 在你第一次运行 `cargo build` 时创建 *Cargo.lock* 文件，所以现在 *guessing_game* 目录中就有这个文件。

en: When you build a project for the first time, Cargo figures out all the versions of the dependencies that fit the criteria and then writes them to the *Cargo.lock* file. When you build your project in the future, Cargo will see that the *Cargo.lock* file exists and will use the versions specified there rather than doing all the work of figuring out versions again. This lets you have a reproducible build automatically. In other words, your project will remain at 0.10.1 until you explicitly upgrade, thanks to the *Cargo.lock* file. Because the *Cargo.lock* file is important for reproducible builds, it’s often checked into source control with the rest of the code in your project.
zh: 当你第一次构建项目时，Cargo 会找出符合条件的所有依赖版本，然后将它们写入 *Cargo.lock* 文件。以后构建项目时，Cargo 会看到 *Cargo.lock* 文件存在，并使用其中指定的版本，而不是再次做找出所有版本的工作。这让你自动获得可重现的构建。换句话说，得益于 *Cargo.lock* 文件，你的项目会保持在 0.10.1，直到你显式升级。由于 *Cargo.lock* 文件对可重现构建很重要，它通常会和项目中的其他代码一起提交到源代码控制中。

zh: #### 更新 crate 以获得新版本

en: When you *do* want to update a crate, Cargo provides the command `update`, which will ignore the *Cargo.lock* file and figure out all the latest versions that fit your specifications in *Cargo.toml*. Cargo will then write those versions to the *Cargo.lock* file. Otherwise, by default, Cargo will only look for versions greater than 0.10.1 and less than 0.11.0. If the `rand` crate has released the two new versions 0.10.2 and 0.999.0, you would see the following if you ran `cargo update`:

en: Let’s start using `rand` to generate a number to guess. The next step is to update *src/main.rs*, as shown in Listing 2-3.
zh: 让我们开始使用 `rand` 生成一个用于猜测的数字。下一步是更新 *src/main.rs*，如代码清单 2-3 所示。

en: First, we add the line `use rand::prelude::*;`. The `prelude` module contains the most commonly used parts of the `rand` crate, and `use` makes those items available in our program’s scope.
zh: 首先，我们添加 `use rand::prelude::*;` 这一行。`prelude` 模块包含 `rand` crate 中最常用的部分，`use` 使这些项在程序作用域中可用。

en: Next, we’re adding two lines in the middle. In the first line, we call the `rand::rng` function that gives us the particular random number generator we’re going to use: one that is local to the current thread of execution and is seeded by the operating system. Then, we call the `random_range` method on the random number generator. This method is defined by the `RngExt` trait that is part of the `rand::prelude` module that we brought into scope with the `use rand::prelude::*;` statement. The `random_range` method takes a range expression as an argument and generates a random number in the range. The kind of range expression we’re using here takes the form `start..=end` and is inclusive on the lower and upper bounds, so we need to specify `1..=100` to request a number between 1 and 100.
zh: 接下来，我们在中间添加两行。第一行中，我们调用 `rand::rng` 函数，它给我们提供将要使用的特定随机数生成器：一个位于当前执行线程本地、由操作系统播种的生成器。然后，我们在该随机数生成器上调用 `random_range` 方法。该方法由 `RngExt` trait 定义，而该 trait 属于我们通过 `use rand::prelude::*;` 语句引入作用域的 `rand::prelude` 模块。`random_range` 方法接受一个范围表达式作为参数，并生成该范围内的随机数。我们这里使用的范围表达式形式为 `start..=end`，包含上下界，因此需要指定 `1..=100` 来请求 1 到 100 之间的数字。

en: ## Comparing the Guess to the Secret Number
zh: ## 将猜测与秘密数字进行比较

en: Now that we have user input and a random number, we can compare them. That step is shown in Listing 2-4. Note that this code won’t compile just yet, as we will explain.
zh: 现在我们有了用户输入和一个随机数，可以比较它们了。这一步如代码清单 2-4 所示。请注意，这段代码暂时还不能编译，原因我们将会解释。

en: First, we add another `use` statement, bringing a type called `std::cmp::Ordering` into scope from the standard library. The `Ordering` type is another enum and has the variants `Less`, `Greater`, and `Equal`. These are the three outcomes that are possible when you compare two values.
zh: 首先，我们再添加一个 `use` 语句，把标准库中名为 `std::cmp::Ordering` 的类型引入作用域。`Ordering` 类型是另一个枚举，具有 `Less`、`Greater` 和 `Equal` 三个变体。它们是比较两个值时可能出现的三种结果。

en: Then, we add five new lines at the bottom that use the `Ordering` type. The `cmp` method compares two values and can be called on anything that can be compared. It takes a reference to whatever you want to compare with: Here, it’s comparing `guess` to `secret_number`. Then, it returns a variant of the `Ordering` enum we brought into scope with the `use` statement. We use a [`match`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-02-match.html) expression to decide what to do next based on which variant of `Ordering` was returned from the call to `cmp` with the values in `guess` and `secret_number`.
zh: 然后，我们在底部添加五行新代码，使用 `Ordering` 类型。`cmp` 方法比较两个值，可以在任何可比较的对象上调用。它接受一个对你想要比较的对象的引用：这里它把 `guess` 与 `secret_number` 进行比较。之后，它返回我们用 `use` 语句引入作用域的 `Ordering` 枚举的一个变体。我们使用 [`match`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch06-02-match.html) 表达式，根据用 `guess` 和 `secret_number` 的值调用 `cmp` 所返回的 `Ordering` 变体，决定接下来做什么。

en: A `match` expression is made up of *arms*. An arm consists of a *pattern* to match against, and the code that should be run if the value given to `match` fits that arm’s pattern. Rust takes the value given to `match` and looks through each arm’s pattern in turn. Patterns and the `match` construct are powerful Rust features: They let you express a variety of situations your code might encounter, and they make sure you handle them all. These features will be covered in detail in Chapter 6 and Chapter 19, respectively.
zh: `match` 表达式由*分支*（arm）组成。一个分支由一个*模式*（pattern）和如果传给 `match` 的值符合该分支模式时应运行的代码组成。Rust 取出传给 `match` 的值，依次检查每个分支的模式。模式和 `match` 构造是强大的 Rust 特性：它们让你表达代码可能遇到的各种情况，并确保你处理所有情况。这些特性将分别在第 6 章和第 19 章详细介绍。

en: Let’s walk through an example with the `match` expression we use here. Say that the user has guessed 50 and the randomly generated secret number this time is 38.
zh: 让我们用一个例子来走查这里使用的 `match` 表达式。假设用户猜的是 50，而这次随机生成的秘密数字是 38。

en: When the code compares 50 to 38, the `cmp` method will return `Ordering::Greater` because 50 is greater than 38. The `match` expression gets the `Ordering::Greater` value and starts checking each arm’s pattern. It looks at the first arm’s pattern, `Ordering::Less`, and sees that the value `Ordering::Greater` does not match `Ordering::Less`, so it ignores the code in that arm and moves to the next arm. The next arm’s pattern is `Ordering::Greater`, which *does* match `Ordering::Greater`! The associated code in that arm will execute and print `Too big!` to the screen. The `match` expression ends after the first successful match, so it won’t look at the last arm in this scenario.
zh: 当代码比较 50 与 38 时，`cmp` 方法会返回 `Ordering::Greater`，因为 50 大于 38。`match` 表达式获得 `Ordering::Greater` 值，开始检查每个分支的模式。它查看第一个分支的模式 `Ordering::Less`，发现值 `Ordering::Greater` 不匹配 `Ordering::Less`，于是忽略该分支中的代码，转到下一个分支。下一个分支的模式是 `Ordering::Greater`，它*确实*匹配 `Ordering::Greater`！该分支中关联的代码将执行，并向屏幕打印 `Too big!`。`match` 表达式在第一次成功匹配后结束，因此在这个场景中不会查看最后一个分支。

en: However, the code in Listing 2-4 won’t compile yet. Let’s try it:


en: The core of the error states that there are *mismatched types*. Rust has a strong, static type system. However, it also has type inference. When we wrote `let mut guess = String::new()`, Rust was able to infer that `guess` should be a `String` and didn’t make us write the type. The `secret_number`, on the other hand, is a number type. A few of Rust’s number types can have a value between 1 and 100: `i32`, a 32-bit number; `u32`, an unsigned 32-bit number; `i64`, a 64-bit number; as well as others. Unless otherwise specified, Rust defaults to an `i32`, which is the type of `secret_number` unless you add type information elsewhere that would cause Rust to infer a different numerical type. The reason for the error is that Rust cannot compare a string and a number type.
zh: 错误的核心说明存在*类型不匹配*。Rust 拥有强大的静态类型系统。不过，它也有类型推断。当我们写 `let mut guess = String::new()` 时，Rust 能够推断 `guess` 应该是 `String`，而无需我们写出类型。另一方面，`secret_number` 是数字类型。Rust 的几种数字类型都可以保存 1 到 100 之间的值：`i32`（32 位数字）、`u32`（无符号 32 位数字）、`i64`（64 位数字）等。除非另有说明，Rust 默认使用 `i32`，这就是 `secret_number` 的类型，除非你在别处添加类型信息让 Rust 推断出不同的数值类型。错误的原因是 Rust 无法比较字符串和数字类型。

We’ll cover this in more detail in [Chapter 3](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch03-01-variables-and-mutability.html#shadowing), but for now, know that this feature is often used when you want to convert a value from one type to another type.

en: The `parse` method will only work on characters that can logically be converted into numbers and so can easily cause errors. We’ll treat this `Result` the same way by using the `expect` method again. If `parse` returns an `Err` `Result` variant because it couldn’t create a number from the string, the `expect` call will crash the game and print the message we give it. en: We switch from an `expect` call to a `match` expression to move from crashing on an error to handling the error. Remember that `parse` returns a `Result` type and `Result` is an enum that has the variants `Ok` and `Err`. We’re using a `match` expression here, as we did with the `Ordering` result of the `cmp` method.
zh: 我们将 `expect` 调用改为 `match` 表达式，从遇错即崩溃转为处理错误。记住，`parse` 返回一个 `Result` 类型，而 `Result` 是一个具有 `Ok` 和 `Err` 变体的枚举。我们在这里使用 `match` 表达式，就像处理 `cmp` 方法返回的 `Ordering` 结果时那样。

en: If `parse` is able to successfully turn the string into a number, it will return an `Ok` value that contains the resultant number. That `Ok` value will match the first arm’s pattern, and the `match` expression will just return the `num` value that `parse` produced and put inside the `Ok` value. That number will end up right where we want it in the new `guess` variable we’re creating.
zh: 如果 `parse` 能成功将字符串转换为数字，它会返回一个包含结果数字的 `Ok` 值。该 `Ok` 值将匹配第一个分支的模式，`match` 表达式将返回 `parse` 生成并放入 `Ok` 值中的 `num` 值。这个数字最终会进入我们正在创建的新 `guess` 变量中我们想要的位置。

en: If `parse` is *not* able to turn the string into a number, it will return an `Err` value that contains more information about the error. The `Err` value does not match the `Ok(num)` pattern in the first `match` arm, but it does match the `Err(_)` pattern in the second arm. The underscore, `_`, is a catch-all value; in this example, we’re saying we want to match all `Err` values, no matter what information they have inside them. So, the program will execute the second arm’s code, `continue`, which tells the program to go to the next iteration of the `loop` and ask for another guess. So, effectively, the program ignores all errors that `parse` might encounter!
zh: 如果 `parse` *不能*将字符串转换为数字，它会返回一个包含更多错误信息的 `Err` 值。`Err` 值不匹配第一个 `match` 分支中的 `Ok(num)` 模式，但它匹配第二个分支中的 `Err(_)` 模式。下划线 `_` 是一个通配值；在这个例子中，我们表示要匹配所有 `Err` 值，无论它们内部包含什么信息。因此，程序会执行第二个分支的代码 `continue`，它告诉程序进入 `loop` 的下一次迭代并请求再次猜测。所以，实际上程序忽略了 `parse` 可能遇到的所有错误！
